correctness.rationale: Reconstructed CRT equality gamma(k,N)=max prime-power gamma via coordinatewise padding. For p=3 the cyclic unit group has k-th power subgroup u=1 mod M; nonunit k-th powers vanish at modulus 3^(s+2), so target M needs M unit summands for a>=s+2. Unit image and ones give matching upper bound, and a<=s+1 only residues 0,1 occur. For p=2, v2(k)=1 and unit k-th powers are precisely 1 mod8; mod16 target 8 needs 8. For p>=5 Cauchy-Davenport on H union {0} covers F_p in k terms, add a unit summand to ensure nonzero derivative and Hensel-lift with p not dividing k. M>max(k+1,8). Independent exhaustive residue BFS confirms k=6 mod 9 gamma=8, mod27 gamma=9, mod81 gamma=9, mod16 gamma=8; k=18 mod27 gamma=26 and mod81 gamma=27. These finite instances are not the universal proof.
residual_risks: Finite tests are not proofs of the whole s-family.
